name: SearchMiner
author: yodsira

sections.description:
SearchMiner is a passive observer for your site search. It records what
visitors search for, flags every search that returned zero results and shows
searches where visitors got results but clicked nothing — the quiet revenue
leak most sites never measure.

It does not replace your search. Keep the search you already have (native
WordPress search, WooCommerce product search) — SearchMiner simply tells you
what it is missing.

Highlights:

  • Top searches, top zero-result searches and top “searched but clicked nothing” queries
  • Searches per day chart with the zero-result share highlighted
  • WooCommerce aware: product searches are marked separately
  • Dashboard widget: the zero-result searches your visitors made most
  • Privacy first: no IP addresses, no user accounts stored; automatic retention
    (30–365 days); one-click erase of all recorded searches
  • Bots and crawlers are filtered out, so numbers mean people
  • No data leaves your server

How it works

When a visitor loads a search results page, SearchMiner records the phrase
and the number of results. If result tracking is enabled, a tiny script on
the results page sends one beacon when the visitor clicks a result — or one
beacon when they leave without clicking anything. That is all.

Limitations (honest list)

  • Searches served entirely from a full-page cache bypass PHP and are not recorded
  • AJAX search widgets (third-party) are not recorded in this version
  • The plugin counts behaviour; it cannot tell you visitor intent

Pro Version

An optional companion plugin adds (one license = one site, 12 months of updates):

  • Typo clustering — groups misspellings (“snearkers”) with the real query
  • Revenue-at-risk matching — links zero-result searches to existing products
  • Weekly email digest with the top fixes for your shop

The free version is fully functional on its own and never limited.
Details: https://yodsira.com/product/searchminer/

External Services

By default the free plugin makes no outgoing requests: SearchMiner stores
search phrases in your own database. The only developer connection is the
optional, off-by-default error telemetry described at the end of this
section — nothing is sent until you enable it yourself.

For transparency: the package ships a shared Telegram delivery helper that
stays completely inert in the free version and is only activated by the
optional SearchMiner Pro companion (a separate plugin). If you enable
Telegram delivery in Pro, that helper talks to api.telegram.org — the
Telegram Bot API — using the bot token you configure yourself.
Terms: https://telegram.org/tos — Privacy: https://telegram.org/privacy
* Optional, off by default: anonymous error reports. If the admin enables
the checkbox in the plugin settings, a daily batch of sanitized error
signatures (message, file name:line, culprit plugin/theme, first stack
frames, plugin/WP/PHP versions, site address) is sent to
https://yodsira.com/api/telemetry so bugs can be reproduced and fixed.
Nothing is sent while the checkbox is off.
Why: I am an independent developer, and this is the only way I learn about
bugs I cannot reproduce myself. The free plugin makes no requests at all
until you enable this option; when an error happens, an anonymous
signature is sent to yodsira.com so I can fix it in the next release.
Nothing else ever leaves your site, and you can switch it off at any
moment. Every report is read by a human.
Example of exactly what one report looks like (sanitized):

`message: “Call to a member function get_id() on null” — file: file.php:123 — culprit: plugin other-plugin — versions: plugin 0.2.5, WordPress 6.8, PHP 8.2
That is the whole payload — no content, no user data, no usage tracking.
Disabling telemetry clears any queued reports immediately.
Developer service terms: https://yodsira.com/en/terms/
Privacy policy: https://yodsira.com/en/privacy/
sections.installation:
1. Install via Plugins → Add New → search for “SearchMiner”, or upload the zip.
  2. Activate. That is it — capture starts immediately.
  3. Open SearchMiner in the admin menu after some searches have happened.
sections.faq:
Does it replace my search?

No. SearchMiner observes any search based on the standard WordPress search
query, including WooCommerce product search.

Do you store IP addresses or personal data?

No IP addresses are stored. The plugin records search phrases, counts and
timestamps only. Retention is configurable (30–365 days) and everything can
be erased with one click.

Will it slow my site down?

Capture is a single indexed upsert that runs only on search pages. Nothing
runs on regular page views.

Does it work with Relevanssi / Ivory Search / FiboSearch?

If those plugins use the standard WordPress search query, SearchMiner sees
it. Purely AJAX third-party search widgets are not recorded in this version.
sections.changelog:
0.2.6

  • Update: “Send anonymous report to developer” — confirmation dialog,
    sending once never enables telemetry; disabling telemetry clears any
    queued reports immediately.
  • Update: telemetry transparency — developer rationale in the settings block
    and readme, a sanitized example of exactly one report, and an always-visible
    “Send error report now” button (manual, conscious sending).

0.2.5

  • New: optional, OFF by default anonymous error telemetry (daily batch of
    sanitized signatures to yodsira.com/api/telemetry, disclosed in External
    Services; nothing is sent until the admin opts in).
  • Readme: privacy wording aligned with the optional telemetry
    (no absolute “never sends” claims anywhere).

0.2.4

  • New: Yodsira Admin UI Standard — design tokens, WCAG-checked palette
    (brand mint decor-only), collapsible settings, quiet Pro side card.
  • New: welcome card instead of empty charts when no searches are recorded
    yet; live search stats as badges next to the title.
  • New: a one-time contextual notice on the plugin’s own pages (day 7, at most
    twice ever) inviting a wp.org rating or a support-forum report; fully
    dismissible, no tracking.

0.2.3

  • New: a “Pro” screen in the admin menu describing the optional SearchMiner
    Pro companion (typo clustering, revenue-at-risk matching, weekly digests).
  • Readme: the Pro section now lists the concrete companion features.

0.2.2

  • New: CSV export of the recorded queries (the current range) from the Overview page.
  • New: a SearchMiner section in Tools → Site Health → Info (capture status,
    searches and zero-result rate for the last 30 days, retention).
  • Fix: the dashboard widget now shows an honest “capture is disabled” note
    instead of stale data when recording is turned off in the settings.
  • Readme: the External Services section now states it accurately — the free
    plugin makes no outgoing requests; the bundled Telegram helper is inert
    until the Pro companion activates it.

0.2.1

  • Accuracy: a search is counted once — viewing results pages 2, 3, … no longer inflates the counter.
  • Charts: days without searches are now shown as zero instead of being skipped (sparse traffic no longer looks like consecutive busy days).
  • Internal: removed a dead duplicate registration of the searchminer_zero_queries filter.
  • Fixed: the internal version constant (used for asset cache-busting) had been stuck at 0.1.1 since the first release — it is now derived from the plugin header.

0.1.4

  • Fix: dashboard top-lists could render empty on some MySQL versions.

0.1.2

  • Load the shared Yodsira family components (family status endpoint).

0.1.0

  • Initial release: capture, dashboard, settings, privacy tools, click tracking.
